summary:
GALE EXPLORER is a project designed to help astronauts better navigate the surface of Mars. Our project focuses on Gale Crater, an area of Mars that NASA's Curiosity rover has been exploring for years.
This project brought together different types of NASA data together in one place so that astronauts can get a better idea of what the Martian surface actually looks like and can be evaluated to traverse. Elevation data from HRSC was used to create a 3D model of Gale Crater, detailed images from the HiRISE camera were used to show the surface, and Curiosity's actual travel route to show where the rover has explored.
details:
GALE EXPLORER combines datasets like the HRSC heightmap and the Curiosity Rover Path to give future astronauts a way to look around the terrain and understand the challenges they might face when exploring Mars. Our goal is to make it easier to study the landscape, identify interesting areas, and think about where astronauts could travel and conduct research.

This project is an early demonstration of how different NASA datasets can work together to make Mars exploration easier to understand and plan for. In the future, we hope to add more information and tools to make it even more useful for scientists, researchers, and future Mars explorers.
